name.text: Three-set survey with an unknown centre

questiontext.text:
\({@N@}\) learners at a school in {@town@} were asked how they travelled during the last week: by matatu (\(M\)), by boda boda (\(B\)) or on foot (\(W\)). \({@nA@}\) used a matatu, \({@nB@}\) a boda boda and \({@nC@}\) walked.

\({@r2@}\) used a matatu and a boda boda but did not walk; \({@r4@}\) used a matatu and walked but no boda boda; \({@r6@}\) used a boda boda and walked but no matatu. \({@r8@}\) used none of these.

(a) How many used all three? [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) How many used a matatu only? [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Let \(x\) learners use all three. The exactly two regions are given, so each only region is a set total minus its two exactly two regions minus \(x\):

matatu only \({@nA@} - {@r2@} - {@r4@} - x = {@ka@} - x\); boda boda only \({@nB@} - {@r2@} - {@r6@} - x = {@kb@} - x\); on foot only \({@nC@} - {@r4@} - {@r6@} - x = {@kc@} - x\).

Adding all eight regions:

\[({@ka@} - x) + ({@kb@} - x) + ({@kc@} - x) + {@r2@} + {@r4@} + {@r6@} + x + {@r8@} = {@N@}\]

so \({@S@} - 2x = {@N@}\), \(2x = {@x2@}\) and \(x = {@x@}\).

(a) \({@x@}\) used all three. (b) Matatu only \(= {@ka@} - {@x@} = {@r1@}\).

Check that no region is negative and that each set total is right, for example matatu \({@r1@} + {@r2@} + {@r4@} + {@x@} = {@nA@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Sets: three-set surveys with an unknown centre

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 1.1 (e): Find the number in all three of three groups from the set totals, the exactly-two counts and the number in none, and then an only region.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from the miscellaneous revision exercises (26 boys and three languages) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: finding the number in all three sets of a survey; exactly-two counts are given instead of pair totals, transport in Kenya, every number new.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Look again at the last step of your equation. Adding the eight regions takes \(x\) away three times and adds it once, so the equation has \(2x\) in it, not \(x\).

falsefeedback.text: Let \(x\) use all three. Write each only region in \(x\), add all eight regions and set the sum equal to \({@N@}\).

truefeedback.text: Matatu only must also leave out those who used all three.
Your method is right, but it uses your answer to (a), which is not right.

qtest.description: Twice x; matatu only follows from it
